AgentReadResult.x-cognia-wire-source: crate::agents::commands::AgentReadResult. NOTE: no rename_all — the fields stay snake_case on the wire, and only parse_error is renamed (to parseError) alongside skip_serializing_if.

parsed.x-cognia-opaque-reason: serde_json::Value — the agent's own config tree, whose shape is owned by that vendor's format, not by this contract. Deliberately unconstrained; the envelope around it is not.

AgentWriteResult.x-cognia-wire-source: crate::agents::commands::AgentWriteResult. backup_path is renamed to backupPath and skipped when None.

condition.description: Discriminated by `kind`; the per-kind fields are declared open (BackgroundMonitorCondition).

CodeServerStatus.description: `profile` is absent only when talking to a pre-platform host during a rolling upgrade; `relayPath` never carries a credential or the host loopback port.

config.x-cognia-opaque-reason: The stored ExternalAgentConfig is owned by the external-agent domain and versioned with it; this plane owns the head/revision envelope around it, which is typed above.

FleetSnapshot.x-cognia-wire-source: crate::fleet::registry::FleetSnapshot (rename_all = camelCase), via rpc/diagnostics.rs `to_json(runtime().snapshot_for_tenant(..))`. hosts and runtimeCapabilities carry skip_serializing_if = Vec::is_empty, so both are absent — not empty arrays — on a quiet host.
FleetSnapshot.x-cognia-fixes: Previously LegacyList, which requires an ARRAY. FleetSnapshot is a struct and always serializes as an object, so the enforced output contract rejected every fleet_get_snapshot response with contract_output_violation. The helper directly above the dispatch arm (fleet_event_payload) already asserted 'fleet snapshot must serialize as an object'.

items.x-cognia-opaque-reason: FleetSession is owned by the Agent Fleet domain (ADR-0009) and is projected from several agent runtimes. The envelope is pinned here; item-level typing belongs with that domain and is tracked as remaining response-schema debt.

FleetWorkerEnrollment.x-cognia-wire-source: Literal json! in the fleet_worker_enrollment_create arm; `enrollment` is the String returned by SecurityStore::create_worker_enrollment.

FleetWorkerList.x-cognia-wire-source: Vec<WorkerDeviceSummary>. NOTE serde(flatten): DeviceSummary's fields are inlined ALONGSIDE hostRef rather than nested under a `device` key.

GitDiff.description: Rust never sends `language`; the renderer derives it from the path extension after receipt.

GitStackBranchPairList.x-cognia-wire-source: Vec<(String, String)> — a Rust tuple serialises as a two-element JSON array, not an object.

IntegrationSpoolDelivery.x-cognia-wire-source: crates/cognia-scheduling/src/workflow/integration_spool.rs SpoolDelivery (serde rename_all = camelCase). `eventType` carries no skip_serializing_if, so it is always present and null when the route declares no event-type header.

LarkEntryToken.x-cognia-wire-source: lark_entry::rpc_entry_issue. Two branches: kind=entry returns token+jti+expiresAt, kind=surface returns token alone — so only `token` is guaranteed.

LarkMetricAck.x-cognia-wire-source: lark_entry::rpc_metrics_record — json!({ "ok": true }). An unknown metric name is an Err, so `ok` is only ever literal true.

LegacyList.x-cognia-opaque-reason: The command serializes an existing domain collection; item compatibility remains owned by that domain.

LegacyRecord.x-cognia-opaque-reason: The command serializes an existing domain record whose stable root is an object; property-level compatibility remains owned by that domain.

LegacyResult.x-cognia-opaque-reason: The legacy dispatch seam intentionally carries provider-, plugin-, or bridge-defined JSON. The command remains contract-covered at the JSON value boundary until its owning domain publishes a narrower stable wire type.

items.x-cognia-wire-source: cognia_observability::log_query::NativeLogEntry. epochMs and fields carry skip_serializing_if = Option::is_none, so both are absent rather than null.

fields.x-cognia-opaque-reason: serde_json::Value — arbitrary structured fields captured at the log call site.

NullableStringResult.x-cognia-wire-source: Option<String> — null means absent-at-that-ref or binary, which is an ordinary answer rather than an error.

PluginApiCapability.x-cognia-wire-source: crates/cognia-plugin-runtime/src/api_bridge.rs PluginApiCapability (serde rename_all = camelCase), returned as a list by plugin_get_capabilities_for_host.

PluginRuntimeSnapshot.x-cognia-wire-source: crates/cognia-plugin-runtime/src/lib.rs PluginRuntimeSnapshot. NOTE: no rename_all — the fields stay snake_case on the wire. The two Option fields carry no skip_serializing_if, so they are always present as null.

RawWorkspaceEntry.description: snake_case on the wire — the Rust side does not rename these; the client maps them via fromRawWorkspaceEntry.

ScheduledTask.description: Date fields cross the wire as ISO-8601 strings; the client rehydrates them via hydrateTask. Optional fields are omitted rather than sent as null.

ScheduledTaskPayload.description: Union whose first member is Record<string, unknown> (types/scheduler): the per-task-type payload shapes are refinements, so any object is valid on the wire.

SecretValue.x-cognia-wire-source: Option<String> from cognia_secrets::keyring_secrets::get, via rpc/chat.rs `to_json(value)`. null means the key is absent — a successful read, not an error.
SecretValue.x-cognia-fixes: Previously LegacyRecord, which requires an object. Every successful secret_store_get / keyring_secret_get response is a bare string or null, so the enforced output contract rejected all of them with contract_output_violation.

SidecarStatus.x-cognia-wire-source: crate::claude::commands::SidecarStatus — derives Serialize with NO rename_all, and has exactly one field.

TaskExecution.description: Date fields cross the wire as ISO-8601 strings; the client rehydrates them via hydrateExecution.

TerminalExecResult.x-cognia-wire-source: cognia_terminal::exec::TerminalExecResult (serde rename_all = camelCase). A non-zero exit is a SUCCESSFUL response with exitCode set; exitCode is null when the child was signalled or killed on timeout.

TerminalHostSettings.x-cognia-wire-source: crate::terminal_host_service::TerminalHostSettings (serde rename_all = camelCase). The terminal host's own settings file, not part of AppSettings.

TerminalHostStatus.x-cognia-wire-source: crate::terminal_host_bridge::TerminalHostStatus (serde rename_all = camelCase). `descriptor` is skipped for the remote arms — provisioning a device descriptor has no remote path.

TerminalKilledPidList.x-cognia-wire-source: Vec<u32> from cognia_terminal::commands::terminal_kill_port — the PIDs actually signalled, possibly empty when nothing was listening.

TerminalProfileSyncResult.x-cognia-wire-source: rpc/terminal.rs `terminal_host_sync_profiles` — how many profiles the device now owns on the host.

TerminalSession.x-cognia-wire-source: cognia_terminal::host::HostSessionInfo (serde rename_all = camelCase), returned by rpc/terminal.rs via DispatchHost::terminal_list_all. Option fields carry no skip_serializing_if, so they are always present as null — the two ssh_host_key_* fields are the exception and do skip.

TerminalSessionParticipant.x-cognia-wire-source: cognia_terminal::host::SessionParticipant (serde rename_all = camelCase). `deviceId` carries no skip_serializing_if, so it is always present and null for the local desktop.
